value.body_text:
Today, we published a revised edition of Directive 068: Security Deposits.
We made the following revisions to the directive:
Added guidance regarding security deposits for new or amended oilfield waste management facility applications (section 3.1.3).
Revised the notice period for nonrenewal and cancellation of letters of credit from 60 days to 90 days (section 4.2).
Added demand forfeiture bonds (DFBs) to the list of acceptable forms of security (section 4.3). We will now accept surety bonds in the form of an AER-approved DFB from licensees of oil, gas, geothermal, and brine-hosted mineral developments.
Revised how interest accrued from a cash security deposit is refunded (section 7).
Removed references to monthly bank statements.
The AER-approved DFB is the only form of surety bond accepted by the AER. The DFB will be available on our liability management forms webpage. We will only accept it without alteration.
We will only accept surety from providers with active operations in Canada and an A rating (or equivalent) from a credit-rating agency acceptable to the AER.
The revised edition of Directive 068 is available on the directive landing page.
Direct any questions regarding security deposits to Directive068@aer.ca. All other questions can be directed to our Customer Contact Centre by phone at 403-297-8311 (1-855-297-8311 toll free) or by email at inquiries@aer.ca.
value.subtitle: Revised Edition of Directive 068
value.title: Bulletin 2026-42

value.body_text:
Replaces the previous edition released on July 4, 2023.
Released with Bulletin 2025-04.
See section 1.3 of the directive for what’s new.
Purpose of this Directive
This directive sets out the requirements for completing and submitting a site-specific liability assessment (SSLA). These directive applies to all liability management programs administered under the Oil and Gas Conservation Rules, Brine-Hosted Mineral Resource Development Rules, and Geothermal Resource Development Rules. It does not apply to sites subject to liability management programs administered under the specified enactments (e.g., the Mine Financial Security Program, which is authorized under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act).
The aim of this directive is to improve the consistency and accuracy of liability assessments submitted to the AER. They do not modify requirements on how to provide reasonable care and measures, contamination management (including remediation), suspension, abandonment, and reclamation activities.
Forms and Attachments
Directive 001 Forms
What We Heard

200.description:
One page of an AER publication listing (a Drupal views table): directives, bulletins, hearing decisions, requests for regulatory appeal decisions, participatory and procedural decisions, notices, statistical (ST) reports or news releases. Rows carry the title cell (with its link, often straight to the PDF), the row date (ISO, from the view's `<time>` or the printed `Month D, YYYY`) and every column by its header label. Optional keyword filter and sort; pages are zero-based (10 or 20 rows per page depending on the listing). A keyword that matches nothing returns zero rows with the site's own `No matching records found` notice.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `rows` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cells` | object | Every column of the row keyed by its header label (verbatim cell text). Keys follow `columns`. |
| `date` | string | ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from the row's `<time datetime>`; null when the row has no date cell. |
| `title` | string | Text of the first (title / number) column, e.g. `Directive 056`, `2026 ABAER 009`, `Bulletin 2026-42`. |
| `url` | string | Absolute link of the title cell: the detail page for directives, bulletins, notices and ST reports, the PDF for decisions and orders; null when the cell has no link. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

value.comment_summary: Lemmy is praised for its decentralized, federated structure, and open-source nature, offering a fast, lightweight interface similar to Reddit. Users appreciate the potential to create communities and enjoy fewer trolls, promoting better privacy. However, concerns exist over its lack of a privacy policy, censorship aspects, and inadequate documentation. While some find it a great Reddit alternative, others criticize its user base and lack of certain Reddit features.
value.creator: Dessalines
value.description:
Lemmy is similar to sites like Reddit, Lobste.rs, or Hacker News: you subscribe to forums you're interested in, post links and discussions, then vote, and comment on them. Behind the scenes, it is very different; anyone can easily run a server, and all these servers are federated (think email), and connected to the same universe, called the Fediverse.

For a link aggregator, this means a user registered on one server can subscribe to forums on any other server, and can have discussions with users registered elsewhere.

The overall goal is to create an easily self-hostable, decentralized alternative to Reddit and other link aggregators, outside of their corporate control and meddling.

Each Lemmy server can set its own moderation policy; appointing site-wide admins, and community moderators to keep out the trolls, and foster a healthy, non-toxic environment where all can feel comfortable contributing.

# Features: 
- Open source, AGPL License.
- Self hostable, easy to deploy.
 - Comes with Docker and Ansible.
- Clean, mobile-friendly interface.
- Only username and password are required to sign up!
- User avatar support.
- Live-updating Comment threads.
- Full vote scores (+/-) like old Reddit.
- Themes, including light, dark, and solarized.
- Emojis with autocomplete support. Start typing :
- User tagging using @, Community tagging using !.
- Integrated image uploading in both posts and comments.
- Flexible posts can consist of a title and a combination of self text, URL, or nothing.
- Notifications, on comment replies and when you're tagged.
 - Notifications can be sent via email.
- Private messaging support.
- i18n / internationalization support.
- RSS / Atom feeds for All, Subscribed, Inbox, User, and Community.
- Cross-posting support.
- Automatic related post search when creating new posts. Great for question / answer communities and reposts.
- Moderation abilities.
 - Public Moderation Logs.
 - Can sticky posts to the top of communities.
 - Both site admins, and community moderators, who can appoint other moderators.
 - Can lock, remove, and restore posts and comments.
 - Can ban and unban users from communities and the site.
 - Can transfer site and communities to others.
Can fully erase your data, replacing all posts and comments.
NSFW post / community support.
- High performance.
 - Server is written in rust.
 - Front end is ~80kB gzipped.
 - Supports arm64 / Raspberry Pi.

reviews.body: Lightweight interface that is fast like lightning as well as open source and federated. What is there not to love?

Beware they still have no privacy policy despite being given plenty of links explaining how to create one & appear to be at least somewhat hostile to "right-wingers" which is precisely why a lot of people have left reddit. An alternative with the same issues as the original serves zero purpose.

_[Edited by nathalto, August 16]_

Yet Another Feddi


Like any other flavor of Feddiverse “allows free speech” is their highest moral crime

Probably the most well developed open source reddit alternative, with features added constantly.

reading posts incrementally is still too hard unlike reddit with reddit enhancement suite (which has a few other nice features that lemmy does not have yet).
Cool application but the user base sucks
Lemmy is just as fun and interactive as Reddit, but with better privacy and less trolls.

post.description: Verify device or watchOS compatibility, subscription and in-app purchase prices, the current version or release notes of a specific app.

app_id.description: Numeric App Store app id (the `id` in `apps.apple.com/us/app/<slug>/id493145008`). Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}$.

bundle_id.description: iOS bundle identifier (`com.spotify.client`). Resolved to the app id on the same storefront first. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,254}$.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront code (lowercase, e.g. `us`, `gb`, `de`). Default `us`. Prices and availability are storefront specific. Pattern: ^[a-zA-Z]{2}$.

locale.description: Display locale for names, descriptions and release notes, e.g. `en-US`, `en-GB`. Default `en-US`. Pattern: ^[a-zA-Z]{2,3}(-[a-zA-Z0-9]{2,8})*$.

url.description: A pasted App Store app URL such as `https://apps.apple.com/us/app/headspace-sleep-meditation/id493145008`; the storefront in the path is used unless `country` is given.

value.description:
Welcome to Headspace, your expert-led guide to mental health, mindfulness, and meditation. Whether you're navigating stress, anxiety, sleep trouble, or life’s ups and downs, Headspace is here to support you. Explore science-backed exercises, courses, and programs that help you build everyday skills to care for your mind. For more support, you have access to licensed therapists, mental health coaches or Ebb, your empathetic AI companion. Headspace is always here, so you can always put your mind first.

DAILY MEDITATIONS
Discover mental wellness and mindfulness with over 500+ guided meditations. From quick 3-minute mental resets to longer sessions, we'll help you make meditation a daily practice. Meditate, practice mindfulness and relax. Headspace is proven to increase happiness and reduce stress in just 10 days.

BETTER SLEEP
Headspace helps improve your sleep with expert-led sleep tools, guided sleep meditations, sleep sounds, sleepcasts, and more. Explore sleep music and meditation for sleeping to reduce stress and anxiety.

ANXIETY & STRESS RELIEF
Headspace is the mental health app here to help you manage your stress through personalized recommendations, guided meditations, and exercises. Learn calming breathwork and breathing techniques to help with panic attacks, anxiety relief and calm. Just 2 weeks of Headspace reduces anxiety.

AFFORDABLE THERAPY 
From finding the right therapist to easy scheduling, Headspace therapy makes it easier to start feeling better. You’ll also get access to mindfulness tools and Ebb, your empathetic AI companion, for support anytime you need it. Plus, with partnerships with major insurance companies, your sessions could cost as little as $0.

COACHING & MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORT
Get matched and text with your own mental health coach and schedule sessions at your convenience. Headspace mental health coaches are trained professionals that provide personalized care to help you set and reach goals, manage everyday anxiety and stress, navigate major life events, and more.

WELLNESS & BALANCE
Increase balance with guided meditation and focus music. Calm and relax with quick breathing exercises, improve focus with binaural beats and calm your mind with relaxing music for studying.

MINDFUL MOVEMENT
Relieve stress, release tension, and strengthen your mind-body connection with mindful movement. Practice CBT techniques and CBT therapy exercises to reduce stress and anxiety.

PROGRESS TRACKING
Self-care tracker to follow your mental health journey. Share insights with your mindfulness coach or therapist so they can keep you on track towards your goals.

Headspace is the everyday mental health app that’s proven to help. Stress less, sleep better, and feel happier with do-anywhere exercises and personalized recommendations from Ebb, Headspace’s AI mental health companion.

Access online therapy and psychiatry through your organization.* (Check coverage with your coach or benefits team.)

Start your free trial and experience the benefits of meditation, mindfulness and expert mental health therapy & coaching. Subscription options: $12.99/month, $69.99/year. These prices are for United States, pricing in other countries may vary. Coaching and therapy pricing varies by subscription.

The subscription will automatically renew unless turned off in your iTunes Account Settings at least 24 hours before the current period ends. You can go to your iTunes Account settings to manage your subscription and turn off auto-renew. Your iTunes Account will be charged when the purchase is confirmed. If you subscribe before your free trial ends, the rest of your free trial period will be forfeited as soon as your purchase is confirmed.

Headspace saves your meditation sessions to your Apple Health app.
Read the terms and conditions here: http://www.headspace.com/terms-and-conditions
Read the privacy policy here: https://www.headspace.com/privacy-policy

biography: The Honourable Danielle Smith was sworn-in as Alberta’s 19th Premier on October 11, 2022. She was re-elected as the Member of the Legislative Assembly for the constituency of Brooks-Medicine Hat on May 29, 2023.

Danielle Smith was first elected as the Member of the Legislative Assembly for Highwood on April 23, 2012. She served as leader of the Wildrose Party of Alberta from October 17, 2009, to December 17, 2014.
She previously served on the Special Standing Committee on Members’ Services and the Standing Committee on Alberta’s Economic Future.

Prior to entering politics, Ms. Smith was the director of provincial affairs for Alberta with the Canadian Federation of Independent Business, CFIB. She worked with all levels of government to represent the interests of CFIB’s 10,000 small-business members in Alberta.

Before joining CFIB, Ms. Smith had extensive experience in the media. She was an editorial writer and columnist at the Calgary Herald for six years. She served as host of Global Sunday, a national current affairs television talk show, and was also the host of two programs on CKMX 1060 AM radio in Calgary, Health Frontiers and Standing Ground. She has made frequent guest appearances as a commentator on TV and radio.

Ms. Smith’s public policy experience began with an internship at the Fraser Institute. She was also elected as a trustee for the Calgary board of education and served as the director of the Alberta Property Rights Initiative and the Canadian Property Rights Research Institute.

Smith received a BA in English and a BA in economics from the University of Calgary. She married her husband, David Moretta in 2006 and is the proud stepmother of David’s son Jonathan. Danielle and David live in High River with their two dogs, Caine and Turk.
She was the 814th Member of the Legislative Assembly of Alberta.

ultimos.description:

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 20.

200.description:
Observations of one SGS time series (Sistema Gerenciador de Séries Temporais) by numeric code from api.bcb.gov.br: either the last N observations (`ultimos`, 1..20, the server's maximum) or a date window (`data_inicial`/`data_final`, ISO dates; the server rejects windows longer than 10 years on daily series and requires `data_inicial` for them). Values are returned as the server's decimal strings in `valor` plus a parsed `value` (null when the string is not numeric). Common codes: 432 Selic target, 11 Selic daily, 12 CDI daily, 433 IPCA monthly, 13522 IPCA 12-month, 189 IGP-M, 24364 IBC-Br, 1 USD/BRL PTAX sell. An unknown code is `not_found`; a rejected window is `invalid_input`.

commodity_group_name.description: Exact commodity_group_name, case-insensitive: AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS.

commodity_name.description: Exact commodity_name, case-insensitive (GOLD, WHEAT, NATURAL GAS, BITCOIN).

commodity_subgroup_name.description: Exact commodity_subgroup_name, case-insensitive (GRAINS, PRECIOUS METALS, PETROLEUM AND PRODUCTS, CURRENCIES, STOCK INDICES, ...).

contract_market_code.description: Exact cftc_contract_market_code, a string with leading zeros kept (088691 = GOLD - COMMODITY EXCHANGE INC., 001602 = WHEAT-SRW - CBOT). Discover codes with `markets`. Alone, a code with no rows in this dataset is not_found; combined with date or other filters an empty page is a legitimate empty result. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,12}$.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page of the same query (the SODA $offset).

exchange_code.description: cftc_market_code without its padding: CBT, CME, CMX, NYME, ICUS, ICEU, CMXE, FREX... Matches the padded value the dataset stores ('CMX '). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,4}$.

fields.description: Projection: SODA column names to return (open_interest_all, noncomm_positions_long_all, m_money_positions_long_all, ...). The identity columns id, market_and_exchange_names, report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd and cftc_contract_market_code are always included. An unknown column is invalid_input. Omit for every column.

from.description: Earliest report date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

page_size.description:
Rows per page (a legacy row is ~4.7 KB, a disaggregated row ~7 KB).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000; default 100.

query.description: SODA full-text search ($q) over the text columns, e.g. `gold` or `chicago board of trade`.

report_date.description: One weekly report date (a Tuesday), YYYY-MM-DD. Not combinable with from / to. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

sort.description:
Order by report date then id. The upstream default order is undefined, so an order is always sent.

Provider reference: allowed values ["recent_first", "oldest_first"]; default "recent_first".

to.description: Latest report date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

The identity columns id, market_and_exchange_names, report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd and cftc_contract_market_code are always included. An unknown column is invalid_input. Omit for every column.

from.description: Earliest report date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

page_size.description:
Rows per page (a legacy row is ~4.7 KB, a disaggregated row ~7 KB).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000; default 100.

query.description: SODA full-text search ($q) over the text columns, e.g. `gold` or `chicago board of trade`.

report_date.description: One weekly report date (a Tuesday), YYYY-MM-DD. Not combinable with from / to. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

sort.description:
Order by report date then id. The upstream default order is undefined, so an order is always sent.

Provider reference: allowed values ["recent_first", "oldest_first"]; default "recent_first".

to.description: Latest report date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

200.description:
Filtered data query on any Eurostat dataset through the statistics/1.0 JSON-stat endpoint. Filters are dimension id -> list of codes (OR within a dimension); time is sliced with time, since and until. The sparse JSON-stat cube is flattened into one observation per cell with the codes of every dimension, the value and the Eurostat status flag. Requests that are too large for a synchronous answer fail with upstream_error (413 ASYNCHRONOUS_RESPONSE): narrow the filters.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `observations` as the primary payload key.

| `time` | string |  |
| `value` | number | Null when Eurostat publishes only a status flag (e.g. ':' not available) for the cell. |

limit.description:

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 500.

position.description:
Default ALL.

Provider reference: allowed values ["ALL", "QB", "RB", "WR", "TE", "K", "DST"]; default "ALL".

teams.description:
League size; changes only adp_formatted (round.pick). Default 12.

Provider reference: allowed values ["8", "10", "12", "14"]; default 12.

year.description:
Draft season. Omit for the current season. History starts in 2007 for standard, 2010 for ppr, 2014 for 2qb and rookie, 2015 for dynasty and 2018 for half-ppr; a season without data is not_found.

Provider reference: minimum 2007; maximum 2100.

post.description: This week's start/sit order and projected points for a position in standard, PPR, half-PPR or 2-QB scoring, or long-term dynasty and rookie rankings.

format.description:
standard (non-PPR), ppr, half-ppr or 2qb weekly rankings with projections; dynasty or rookie (dynasty rookie) rankings. 2qb projections use standard scoring. Default ppr.

Provider reference: allowed values ["standard", "ppr", "half-ppr", "2qb", "dynasty", "rookie"]; default "ppr".

limit.description:
Return only the top N. Omit for everything the page lists: the whole table for dynasty, rookie and positions with under 50 players, the site's top 50 for other season-long pages (reported as partial coverage).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 500.

position.description:
ALL (overall), QB, RB, WR, TE, K, DST (team defense) or FLX (RB/WR/TE). Rookie rankings have no K or DST. Season-long pages stop at the site's top 50, so ALL and FLX cover fewer players than the per-position pages together; call QB, RB, WR, TE, K and DST for depth.

Provider reference: allowed values ["ALL", "QB", "RB", "WR", "TE", "K", "DST", "FLX"].

post.description: Before loading or refreshing a copy of the whole PSC register, to learn which daily snapshot is current, fetch its part files elsewhere and check the totals. Per-company PSC reads stay on persons_with_significant_control.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
PSC bulk snapshot version check (source/status) from download.companieshouse.gov.uk/en_pscdata.html: the snapshot date, the single-file snapshot and the N numbered parts with Content-Length, ETag and Last-Modified (HEAD), and the register totals (persons_of_significant_control_count, statements_count, exemptions_count, generated_at) read from the last line of the last part, which is downloaded and inflated. Parts 1 to N-1 (31 to 80 MB compressed, hundreds of MB inflated) and the 2.5 GB single file are beyond what one call may fetch and hold, so their URLs and validators are the hand-off; they are never downloaded. publication_id is <snapshot_date>:<last part ETag>.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `full_snapshot` | object | The single-file snapshot (about 2.5 GB): a hand-off, never downloaded here. |
| `generated_at` | string | Copy of totals.generated_at. |
| `latest_part` | object | The last part, downloaded and inflated in this call to read the totals record. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `page_last_updated` | string | The page's 'Last Updated' text (UK local time, DD/MM/YYYY HH:MMhrs). |
| `part_count` | number | N, the number of numbered parts. |
| `parts` | object[] | Parts 1..N in order. Parts 1..N-1 are hand-offs validated with HEAD and never downloaded (31 to 80 MB compressed, hundreds of MB inflated); part N is downloaded in this call. |
| `publication_id` | string | <snapshot_date>:<last part ETag>; psc_latest_part cursors pin this value. |
| `retrieved_at` | string | RFC 3339 UTC time of the fetch. |
| `snapshot_date` | string | Snapshot date named in the file names. |
| `source_url` | string | The download page that lists the snapshot files. |
| `totals` | object | Register totals from the last line of the last part. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix time in milliseconds when this program read the source. |

| `quests` | object[] | Quests for the instance with their item rewards. |
| `required_level` | number |  |
| `slug` | string |  |
| `status` | string | What the instance is in Forever, like `New instance` or `Classic, new rules`. |
| `type` | string | Dungeon or Raid. |

| `faction_only` | string | alliance or horde when the Group Finder offers it to one faction only. |
| `final_boss` | string |  |
| `loot_known` | boolean | False for instances new in Forever, whose loot is not known yet. |
| `max_level` | number |  |
| `min_level` | number |  |
| `name` | string |  |
| `name_es` | string |  |

| `required_level` | number | Minimum level to enter, when the game sets one. |
| `revealed_at_launch` | boolean | True when the instance is sealed in the beta files and opens at launch. |
| `slug` | string | Chain into `dungeon`. |
| `type` | string | dungeon or raid. |
| `url` | string |  |

200.description:
One World of Warcraft: Forever class spec on one page: what each stat is worth (stat values at level 60), the racials that raise a stat the spec values, the site's calculated pre-raid best in slot at level 60 with item ids and sources, the best flask, elixirs, food and scroll, and the class's crafted Tier 1 set with bonuses.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class` | string |  |

| `data_build` | string | Game client build the site's data comes from, as its footer states. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix time in milliseconds when this program read the source. |
| `pre_raid_bis` | object[] | The site's calculated pre-raid best in slot at level 60 in PvE: one pick per slot. |
| `racials` | object[] | Racials of this class's races that raise a stat the spec values (empty when none does). |
| `role` | string | Role the site gives the spec: Damage, Tank or Healer. |
| `spec` | string |  |

| `tier1` | object | The class's crafted Tier 1 set for the spec: pieces with slots and set bonuses; null when the page has none. |

The response contains the tool result directly.

since_hours_ago.description:
Relative alternative to since: changes in the last N hours (computed from the runner clock, UTC). Not with since.

200.description:
Events modified since a UTC timestamp, from GDACS's own modified-since filter events/geteventlist/latest?datemodified=<since> with alertlevel=green;orange;red, 100 rows per page. The API answers its 404 problem document past the last page (and for a quiet window on page 1); that is an explicit empty page here, not not_found. Rows whose datemodified is before since are dropped with a warning. Each page can take 30+ seconds upstream.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `records` as the primary payload key.

to_date.description: Window end (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD, at most 366 days after from_date. Default: today. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

200.description:
One page (100 rows) of the full GDACS event list for one segment: hazard types x calendar date window, from events/geteventlist/SEARCH with alertlevel=green;orange;red always sent (the API default silently hides Green). Rows are episodes ordered by todate descending; every record carries source_record_id gdacs:<eventtype>:<eventid>:<episodeid>, source_url, publication_id and retrieved_at. publication_id = segment + the newest datemodified on page 1. A window that ended more than 30 days ago is closed: later pages re-fetch page 1 and return invalid_input with issue code publication_changed when the pin moved. A window ending within 30 days of today is live (live: true, coverage partial): rows may shift between pages, so dedupe on source_record_id and reconcile with records_changes. Default segment: the current calendar month to today. Events overlapping the window (long droughts, cyclones) are included even when they started earlier.

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
Full current list of IBM Cloud list prices, one record per plan x deployment (region) x metric x country x quantity tier, walked in catalog order: `GET /api/v1?q=kind:<kind>&_limit=200&_offset=N` (service, iaas, platform_service, composite by default), then `GET /api/v1/{entry}/plan`, then for each plan tagged `paid` `GET /api/v1/{plan}/pricing/deployment` (all pages of 50). The cursor pins the listing ETag and the newest pricing `effective_from` seen; a page that finds a different ETag or a newer `effective_from` fails with `invalid_input` code `publication_changed` instead of mixing versions. Segment key: `entry_id` restricts the walk to one catalog entry. Each page prices at most `plans_per_page` plans and examines at most 20 entries. VPC plans are joined to their `*.profile` entry (vCPU, memory, tenancy). Filters (`regions`, `countries`, `metrics`, `plans_per_page`) are not stored in the cursor: pass them again with `continuation`. Collection contract name: `records/list`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `effective_from` | string | Newest deployment `effective_from` seen so far in the walk; null when no deployment has been priced yet. |
| `entries_examined` | number | Catalog entries visited on this page (including those without paid plans). |
| `entry_id` | string | The segment entry id when the walk is restricted; null for the kind walk. |
| `kinds` | string[] | Kinds walked (empty for an `entry_id` segment). |
| `next_cursor` | string | Opaque cursor for the next page; null when the walk is exhausted. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Observation time (ms since epoch) stamped by the SDK. |
| `plan_count` | number |  |
| `plans` | object[] | Plans priced on this page, in catalog order. |
| `publication_id` | string | Listing ETag pinned by this walk. |
| `record_count` | number |  |
| `records` | object[] | Flattened price rows for the plans on this page. |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |
| `source_url` | string |  |

post.description: Start here for "is Ozempic approved in Canada, under which DINs", "which companies market generic atorvastatin" or "which adalimumab products are marketed" (ATC `L04AB04`), then call `get` with a DIN or drug code for forms, routes, ATC class, status dates, company address and the monograph.

company.description: Company (DIN owner) name or part of it, e.g. `novo nordisk`, `pfizer canada`. Narrows `query`, or lists a company's products on its own; short generic names such as `pharma` match thousands of products and can time out.

limit.description:
Results per page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 25; default 10.

offset.description:
`next_offset` from the previous page; repeat the same query, company and status with it.

Provider reference: minimum 0; default 0.

query.description: A brand name or active ingredient (`Ozempic`, `semaglutide`, `atorvastatin calcium`), a DIN (`02471469`), an ATC code or prefix of at least four characters (`L04AB04`, `L04AB`) or a 10-digit AIG number. The kind is inferred. Text matches anywhere in brand names and in active ingredient names, and both result sets are merged.

status.description:
`active`: Approved, Marketed or Dormant, the statuses Health Canada counts as active DINs. `cancelled`: every cancelled status plus revoked or expired interim-order authorizations. `any` (default) also includes Restricted Access.

Provider reference: allowed values ["any", "active", "marketed", "approved", "dormant", "cancelled"]; default "any".

200.description:
Find drug products in Health Canada's Drug Product Database by brand name or active ingredient, DIN, WHO ATC code, active ingredient group (AIG) number or company, optionally limited to active, marketed, approved, dormant or cancelled products. Each result has the DIN and drug code, brand name and descriptor, company, class, current status, schedules, every active ingredient with its strength, the AIG number and whether a product monograph is on file. | `source_url` | string | The product's DPD page. |

value.description:
Van Rijswijk Tweewielers, Al 109 jaar de fietsenmaker van Tilburg.

Sinds 2015 mag Van Rijswijk Tweewielers zich bij Koninklijke Beschikking Hofleverancier noemen wegens het lange bestaan.

Dé plaats voor nieuwe fietsen, elektrische fietsen, occasions, reparatie en deskundig advies.

Wij dealer van de volgende merken:

Fietsen, elektrische fietsen en bakfietsen:

- Trek
- Advanced Ebike Das Original
- Cortina
- Urban Arrow
- Van Raam aangepaste fietsen

Verder heeft Van Rijswijk Tweewielers een breed assortiment accessoires en onderdelen op voorraad voor fietsen, bromfietsen, oldtimers en scooters.

In onze ruim uitgeruste werkplaats repareren wij alle merken fietsen, elektrische fietsen en bakfietsen.

Als uw tweewieler schade heeft kunnen wij hiervan een schade expertise maken wat geaccepteerd wordt door alle verzekerings maatschapijen.

Als uw tweewieler defect is en u kunt hem zelf niet na onze werkplaats brengen voor reparatie hebben wij ook een ophaal service, Neem hiervoor contact op met ons om een afspraak te maken.

U kunt bij ons ook een verzekering afsluiten voor uw tweewieler, Wij zijn een volmachtbedrijf van ANWB, Enra en Kingpolis verzekeringen.

Heeft u nog vragen neem dan contact met ons op of kom langs in onze winkel. De koffie staat altijd klaar !

Openingstijden:

Maandag: gesloten
Dinsdag: 09.00 - 18.00
Woensdag: 09.00 - 18.00
Donderdag: 09.00 - 20.00
Vrijdag: 09.00 - 18.00
Zaterdag: 10.30 - 16.30
Zondag: gesloten

Tot ziens bij Van Rijswijk Tweewielers sinds 1913 uw fietsenmaker.

Zoekwoorden:fiets  fietsenmaker tilburg gazelle batavus sparta merida pepper cube

post.description: Finding second-hand or new items for sale in the Netherlands: call with a query, then narrow with category_id/subcategory_id from categories, filters from filters, min_price/max_price, postcode/distance_km, condition or sort. Take listing_id into listing for the full description, bids and seller profile.

category_id.description:
Top-level category id from a previous result's categories (an entry with parent_id null), e.g. 445 Fietsen en Brommers.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 99999999.

condition.description: Item condition (Nieuw, Zo goed als nieuw, Gebruikt, Refurbished, Niet werkend); several values match any of them. Same as filters {"condition": [...]}.

distance_km.description:
Only listings within this many km of postcode; needs postcode.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 300.

filters.description: Chosen filters as key/value pairs: keys are a returned filter's key, values one of its values[].value (or an array of them for multi_select filters). Example: {"delivery": "Verzenden", "offeredSince": "Een week", "storage": ["128 GB", "256 GB"]}. A key or value the search does not offer is rejected as invalid_input.

max_price.description:
Highest price in EUR.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 100000000.

min_price.description:
Lowest price in EUR.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 100000000.

page.description:
Result page, 30 listings per page; pass next_page from the previous result. The site serves at most max_page pages.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200; default 1.

postcode.description: Dutch postcode, e.g. '1012 AB'. Results then carry their distance from it. Pattern: ^[1-9][0-9]{3} ?[A-Za-z]{2}$.

query.description: Search keywords as typed in the Marktplaats search box, e.g. 'fiets' or 'iphone 15'. Optional when category_id is given.

sort.description:
Result order from the site's sort menu: relevance (default), newest or oldest listing date, price low to high, price high to low.

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "newest", "oldest", "price_asc", "price_desc"].

subcategory_id.description:
Subcategory id from categories (an entry whose parent_id is category_id); needs category_id.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 99999999.

200.description:
Search the NEVO food table by name (Dutch or English), synonym or NEVO code, optionally restricted to one food group. Returns one page of foods with their names, group, remark, trace and fortification markers and a chosen set of nutrient values per 100 g (energy, water, protein, fat, carbohydrate, fibre, alcohol, organic acids and ash by default). The site has no server-side search: the program downloads the full table (about 12 MB) and filters it, so each call takes a few seconds.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `foods` as the primary payload key.

offset.description:

The major features of the project are as follows: • Evaluate alternative cross sections: including lane width, shoulders, bike lane, width of planters, sidewalk width, barrier, and retaining wall type. • Develop criteria and select a preferred alternative. • Develop 30%, 60%, 90%, and final design plans, specifications and cost estimates. • Complete environmental study and permitting • Provide design support during construction • Other improvements and work associated with the sidewalk include, but are not limited to, site preparation, erosion and sediment control, storm drainage system, flow control and water quality facilities, environmentally sensitive area impact mitigation, irrigation, landscaping, channelization, retaining walls, signing, traffic control, and other mitigation as required. bids.description: INTRODUCTION The City of Bellevue (the “City”) is requesting competitive proposals from qualified firms for solid waste collection services within the City Service Area. These services include: residential and commercial garbage, recycling, and organics (yard debris and food scraps) collection, the delivery of garbage to a King County facility per the City’s interlocal agreement, and the processing and marketing of collected recyclables and organics. The initial contract term will be for ten (10) years, from July 1, 2028 to June 30, 2038, with a City option for an extension of up to two (2) years. Terms used in this RFP that are defined in the Contract have the meanings assigned to them therein. Defined terms are applicable to both the singular and plural. EXISTING COLLECTION SYSTEM This section generally describes the existing solid waste collection system operated under the current contract. Carefully review Brief Scope of Services, Attachment “A”, and the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A) to determine the scope of operations envisioned under the new Contract. The City’s current contract with Republic Services is available to Proposers upon request. The City of Bellevue has a residential population of approximately 158,000 with approximately 30,800 single-family residential customers and approximately 2,000 multi-family, commercial, and drop-box accounts. The existing collection system is operated under contract with total contractor billings of approximately $37 million in 2025. Garbage collection is voluntary for generators within the City. Single-family Collection Single-family residences are provided weekly garbage collection under a variable rate structure. Under the new contract, Residents will be required to use a contractor-provided garbage cart for basic service, but may use their own containers for extra material. There are approximately 200 single-family residential customers who currently use their own container who will need to transition to a contractor-provided container. Weekly single-family recycling collection is included as part of garbage collection service. Most recyclable materials are placed in the recycling cart except for small appliances and electronics, textiles, and large metal items. Weekly single-family organics (i.e., yard debris and food scraps) collection is also included as part of basic collection services, through the use of 96-gallon carts. Customers may also use Kraft bags and place bundled or boxed materials at the curb as well as rent additional yard debris carts from the Contractor if more than one cart is needed. Customers may set out up to 192 gallons of material per collection, with additional materials accepted for a charge. Non-garbage customers may also subscribe to either or both recycling and organics collection services on a fee-for-service basis. The City has an assignable right to the carts used under the current contract and will assign the ownership of those carts to the Contractor performing services under the new contract. As described in Section 4.1.3 of the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A), bill assistance is to be provided to eligible single-family residential customers by the Contractor billing these Customers a reduced percentage of the regular rate for the subscribed service level. The estimated approximate number of eligible Single-family Residential customers and respective rate reductions are: 70% Rate Reduction: 450 Single-family Residential customers (Senior (62+) households at 50% or less of area median income). 35% Rate Reduction: 1,250 Single-family Residential customers (80% or less of area median income). Commercial and Multi-family Collection Multi-family complexes are provided with commercial garbage services, as well as a recycling and organics program that accepts most of the same materials handled by the single-family recycling program. Commercial and Multi-family Complex garbage collection is provided through the use of customer-owned containers and drop-box compactors, as well as contractor-owned carts, detachable containers, and drop-boxes. A range of sizes and collection frequencies are available. Commercial and Multi-family Complex customers currently are provided unlimited recycling and one hundred ninety-two gallons (192) of organics collection per week, via cart service, per garbage container. The City anticipates offering a bill assistance program for multi-family residents. The planned program has a rebate structure and will be funded and directly implemented by the City. There are no rate reductions for the Contractor to implement in regard to this multi-family resident bill assistance program. Disposal All collected garbage is currently delivered to the King County Disposal System per the City/County Interlocal Agreement. Administration The City is responsible for overall solid waste program administration, including managing the collection contract and providing solid waste education and promotion to the public. These activities are funded through an administrative fee and targeted program fees paid to the City, as provided for in the current contract. This system of funding will change under the new contract to a single annual contract fee paid by the contractor to the City. These programs have traditionally been performed through in-house staff or the use of consultants. The solid waste collection contractor is responsible for providing all services, including, but not limited to, customer service, customer billing, distributing public notices about collection service and schedule changes, such as holiday hours, billing adjustment notices, and other service-related communications, as described in the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A). RFP Exhibits: Exhibit A provides the draft 2028 Contract, which details all the services expected to be performed by the future contractor. Exhibit B provides 2025 collection data by sector/collection program and customer container counts. Exhibit C provides 2026 rates charged by the current contractor to all sectors of customers. Proposal Form 2A provides a listing of service levels desired under the new Contract and customer counts (where available) for services provided under the current contract. The customer counts provided on Form 2A have been reported by the current contractor, and unless noted otherwise in the instructions or footnotes to Proposal Form 2A, are accurate to the best of the City’s knowledge. RFP OBJECTIVES The City has identified the following objectives for future solid waste services: Alignment with best practices Responsive to community needs: reliability, affordability, user experience Compliance with state laws and local policy Leverage technology and data Along with these objectives, the City also intends to maintain key contract elements, including weekly collection services for single-family residents and an embedded rate structure. The RFP structure and terms, sample base contract, proposed alternatives, and evaluation process are intended to support these objectives.
bids.title: RFP #26039 - Solid Waste Services

bids.description: The City is seeking a highly qualified Design-Build Team with progressive design build experience and strong skills in creativity and collaboration that will engage as critical, integrated team members throughout design and construction of a large-scale landscape project (Phase 1) and leading design of the aquatic center (Phase 2). The Bellevue Airfield Park Project (the 'Project') site is located largely within the I-90 commercial district, near the Lake to Lake Trail and major transportation corridors. The Master Plan for this community park includes trails, wooded picnic areas, a playground, splash pad, flexible lawn play, basketball and pickleball courts, and a new regional aquatic center able to support the demand for recreational and competitive swimming in Bellevue and the broader region. The Apprentice Utilization Requirement for the Project will be 15%.
bids.title: RFQ #26020 - Bellevue Airfield Park Project

It is the responsibility of the contractor to provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, disposal, service operations, and expertise required to complete this project for the City of Bellevue in accordance with specifications and site plans. Follow project milestones for ROW landscape inspections checklist, provided at construction pre-con. SEE BID DOCS FOR DETAILED INFOMATION
bids.title: ITQ #26098 - 148th Ave NE, Landscape Renovation

bids.description: This project involves pruning and crown cleaning for up to 168 street trees and removing up to 11 within the northern Bellevue CBD Right-of-Way. Nine trees require only limited dead-wood pruning. Work is time-and-materials with a not-to-exceed limit, and all pruning must follow ISA ANSI A300 and ANSI Z133.1 standards under the supervision of an ISA Certified Arborist, with at least one arborist on-site at all times. Traffic control is required. The City will provide the ROW permit and draft traffic control plans, but the contractor is responsible for all traffic control needed to meet final permit requirements, including any adjustments by the ROW Inspector or needs for Uniformed Police Officers. Contractors must provide all labor, materials, equipment, and disposal necessary to complete the project per City specifications. SEE BID DOCS FOR MORE DETAILS
bids.title: ITQ #26105 - 2026 North CBD Cycle Pruning

Kitchen work includes new equipment and hood and associated structural modifications, roof penetration and installation of hood exhaust, and new cabinets as well as limited electrical, plumbing and mechanical scope. Electrical and plumbing scope require separate trade permit by Contractor. Teen room includes partition demolition, interior door and window reconfiguration and new finishes. Engineer's Estimate Range is $400,000 - $500,000. Attendance at a Pre-Bid site walk/inspection and sign-in by Prime/General Contractors who intend to submit a bid for Work on this project will be held at: 2:00 P.M., October 8th 2026 Crossroads Community Center-16000 NE 10th Bellevue WA 98008

200.description:

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `map_last_modified` | string |  |
| `map_url` | string |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `pages_read` | number |  |
| `publication_id` | string | `archive@sha256:<digest>` of every page's Last-Modified. |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |
| `source_url` | string |  |
| `states` | object[] | Per state in the table: stations found and the pages its listing reads. |
| `stations` | number | Unique stations across the pages read. |
| `status` | string | `current` when no station escapes its state's page set, every station resolves to a state and every table page is on the map. |
| `suggested_pages` | object[] | For each drifting state, the fewest pages that carry all its stations. |
| `table_pages_missing` | string[] | Pages the table reads that the map no longer links. |
| `unassigned` | object[] | Stations with no state in their label, no known coordinates entry and a shared key prefix. |
| `unassigned_count` | number |  |
| `uncovered` | object[] | Stations whose state's page set does not include any page they appear on. |
| `uncovered_count` | number |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
records/list of daily summary rows, one station x month per call (the segment key): GET wea_monsum2.pl and parse its three header lines (the column set varies with the station's sensors: solar, wind average / vector direction / max gust, air and fuel temperature mean/max/min, humidity mean/max/min, dew point, wet bulb, barometric pressure, total precipitation) and one row per day; the Total/Ave./Max./Min. footer is dropped. Blank cells and -9999 sentinels are null. `source_record_id` is `<stn>:<yyyy-mm-dd>`; `publication_id` is the SHA-256 of the parsed rows. A month the archive has no data for returns zero records with the station's inventory of years; an unknown station is not_found. Metric (`M`) by default, English (`E`) on request; months from 2000-01 to the current month.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| `cursor` | string | Resume token pinned to this station, month and publication; calling `daily` with it re-reads the segment and fails with `publication_changed` if the rows changed. |

| `retrieved_at` | string |  |

value.abstract:
Abstract (Overall):
Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a deadly disease whose mechanisms of development remain
incompletely understood. Evidence suggests that pancreatic cancers may arise from acinar cells undergoing a
process called acinar to ductal metaplasia (ADM) or from ductal cells to give rise to Pancreatic Intraepithelial
Neoplasias (PanINs). How mutations or combinations of mutations promote PDAC development and the role of
inflammation in the process still remains unclear. Moreover, interactions between immune cells, cancer-
associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and cancer cells can promote PDAC development and progression, but much
remains to be learned about how signaling between cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME) affects the stem
cell compartment (`stemness') thought to underlie PDAC development and promotes immune evasion. Thus,
multiple questions about fundamental mechanisms governing PDAC development persist.
To address these challenges, our superb and highly interactive team will identify genetic and stromal (immune
cells and CAFs) interactions and pathways that regulate the inception and progression of PDAC using innovative
mouse models and human tissue-based approaches. We propose three Projects to address the following overall
aims:
1. Identify the originating cell(s) and deconstruct genetic pathways underlying PDAC initiation
2. Discover immune signals that cross-talk with epithelial cells and CAFs to promote pancreas cancer
development and stemness
3. Investigate the impact of tumor genetics on PDAC immunobiology and response to macrophage-targeted
immunotherapy
Effort on these projects will be organized through an Administrative and Biostatistics Core (A) and empowered
by two Research Cores, focused on human tissue procurement (Core B), and use of high-dimensional imaging
to measure cell and signaling interactions in tissues (CODEX; Core C).
The participating investigators on this P01 lead teams that have collaborated productively for years and have
generated compelling preliminary data that support the potential for unraveling the genetic and immune signaling
mechanisms underlying PDAC development, and developing new immunotherapeutic strategies for PDAC,
which has proven frustratingly resistant to immuno-based therapies.
Our studies should broadly impact pancreas cancer biology and importantly, elucidate the reciprocal interactions
between immune and non-immune compartments (epithelial, CAFs) in shaping the tumor microenvironment
during disease evolution. accelerate discovery of novel diagnostic or preventive strategies for early-stage
disease, or therapeutics for advanced PDAC.
value.public_health_relevance:
Project Narrative (Overall):
This P01 application from investigators at Stanford University seeks to discover, apply, and translate science
about pancreatic cancer (PDAC), with the ultimate goal of improving care for patients with this disease. To
address fundamental, persistent questions about the biology of PDAC, we have assembled a superb,
interactive team of productive collaborators to lead our Projects and Research Cores that will identify genetic,
immune cell, and cancer-associated fibroblasts based interactions and pathways that regulate the inception
and progression of PDAC. Advances from studies proposed here could broadly impact pancreas cancer
biology and drive translational efforts in PDAC.

200.description:
Cheap version check of the published file: a 1 KB Range read of UK-Sanctions-List.xml (ETag as publication_id and MD5 content hash, Last-Modified as published_at, total size, the file's DateGenerated) and the gov.uk Content API record (public_updated_at, latest change note, attachment list for every published format). The record count is not returned because it needs the whole 22 MB file; records_list reports total_records on every page.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| `files` | object[] | Every published format on sanctionslist.fcdo.gov.uk. Only the XML is read; bytes, content_type and etag are null for the others (fetching them would spend the WAF rate budget). |
| `govuk` | object | Version metadata from the gov.uk Content API record of the publication (www.gov.uk/api/content/government/publications/the-uk-sanctions-list). |

| `retrieved_at` | string |  |

| `source_url` | string |  |

accepted_answer.body_html:
To understand what yield does, you must understand what generators are. And before you can understand generators, you must understand iterables.

Iterables

When you create a list, you can read its items one by one. Reading its items one by one is called iteration:

>>> mylist = [1, 2, 3]
>>> for i in mylist:
...    print(i)
1
2
3

mylist is an iterable. When you use a list comprehension, you create a list, and so an iterable:

>>> mylist = [x*x for x in range(3)]
>>> for i in mylist:
...    print(i)
0
1
4

Everything you can use "for... in..." on is an iterable; lists, strings, files...

These iterables are handy because you can read them as much as you wish, but you store all the values in memory and this is not always what you want when you have a lot of values.

Generators

Generators are iterators, a kind of iterable you can only iterate over once. Generators do not store all the values in memory, they generate the values on the fly:

>>> mygenerator = (x*x for x in range(3))
>>> for i in mygenerator:
...    print(i)
0
1
4

It is just the same except you used () instead of []. BUT, you cannot perform for i in mygenerator a second time since generators can only be used once: they calculate 0, then forget about it and calculate 1, and end after calculating 4, one by one.

Yield

yield is a keyword that is used like return, except the function will return a generator.

>>> def create_generator():
...    mylist = range(3)
...    for i in mylist:
...        yield i*i
...
>>> mygenerator = create_generator() # create a generator
>>> print(mygenerator) # mygenerator is an object!
<generator object create_generator at 0xb7555c34>
>>> for i in mygenerator:
...     print(i)
0
1
4

Here it's a useless example, but it's handy when you know your function will return a huge set of values that you will only need to read once.

To master yield, you must understand that when you call the function, the code you have written in the function body does not run. The function only returns the generator object, this is a bit tricky.

Then, your code will continue from where it left off each time for uses the generator.

Now the hard part:

The first time the for calls the generator object created from your function, it will run the code in your function from the beginning until it hits yield, then it'll return the first value of the loop. Then, each subsequent call will run another iteration of the loop you have written in the function and return the next value. This will continue until the generator is considered empty, which happens when the function runs without hitting yield. That can be because the loop has come to an end, or because you no longer satisfy an "if/else".

Your code explained

Generator:

# Here you create the method of the node object that will return the generator
def _get_child_candidates(self, distance, min_dist, max_dist):

    # Here is the code that will be called each time you use the generator object:

    # If there is still a child of the node object on its left
    # AND if the distance is ok, return the next child
    if self._leftchild and distance - max_dist < self._median:
        yield self._leftchild

    # If there is still a child of the node object on its right
    # AND if the distance is ok, return the next child
    if self._rightchild and distance + max_dist >= self._median:
        yield self._rightchild

    # If the function arrives here, the generator will be considered empty
    # There are no more than two values: the left and the right children

Caller:

# Create an empty list and a list with the current object reference
result, candidates = list(), [self]

# Loop on candidates (they contain only one element at the beginning)
while candidates:

    # Get the last candidate and remove it from the list
    node = candidates.pop()

    # Get the distance between obj and the candidate
    distance = node._get_dist(obj)

    # If the distance is ok, then you can fill in the result
    if distance <= max_dist and distance >= min_dist:
        result.extend(node._values)

    # Add the children of the candidate to the candidate's list
    # so the loop will keep running until it has looked
    # at all the children of the children of the children, etc. of the candidate
    candidates.extend(node._get_child_candidates(distance, min_dist, max_dist))

return result

This code contains several smart parts:

  • The loop iterates on a list, but the list expands while the loop is being iterated. It's a concise way to go through all these nested data even if it's a bit dangerous since you can end up with an infinite loop. In this case, candidates.extend(node._get_child_candidates(distance, min_dist, max_dist)) exhausts all the values of the generator, but while keeps creating new generator objects which will produce different values from the previous ones since it's not applied on the same node.

  • The extend() method is a list object method that expects an iterable and adds its values to the list.

Usually, we pass a list to it:

>>> a = [1, 2]
>>> b = [3, 4]
>>> a.extend(b)
>>> print(a)
[1, 2, 3, 4]

But in your code, it gets a generator, which is good because:

  1. You don't need to read the values twice.
  2. You may have a lot of children and you don't want them all stored in memory.

And it works because Python does not care if the argument of a method is a list or not. Python expects iterables so it will work with strings, lists, tuples, and generators! This is called duck typing and is one of the reasons why Python is so cool. But this is another story, for another question...

You can stop here, or read a little bit to see an advanced use of a generator:

Controlling a generator exhaustion

>>> class Bank(): # Let's create a bank, building ATMs
...    crisis = False
...    def create_atm(self):
...        while not self.crisis:
...            yield "$100"
>>> hsbc = Bank() # When everything's ok the ATM gives you as much as you want
>>> corner_street_atm = hsbc.create_atm()
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
$100
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
$100
>>> print([corner_street_atm.next() for cash in range(5)])
['$100', '$100', '$100', '$100', '$100']
>>> hsbc.crisis = True # Crisis is coming, no more money!
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
<type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
>>> wall_street_atm = hsbc.create_atm() # It's even true for new ATMs
>>> print(wall_street_atm.next())
<type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
>>> hsbc.crisis = False # The trouble is, even post-crisis the ATM remains empty
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
<type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
>>> brand_new_atm = hsbc.create_atm() # Build a new one to get back in business
>>> for cash in brand_new_atm:
...    print cash
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
...

Note: For Python 3, useprint(corner_street_atm.__next__()) or print(next(corner_street_atm))

It can be useful for various things like controlling access to a resource.

Itertools, your best friend

The itertools module contains special functions to manipulate iterables. Ever wish to duplicate a generator? Chain two generators? Group values in a nested list with a one-liner? Map / Zip without creating another list?

Then just import itertools.

An example? Let's see the possible orders of arrival for a four-horse race:

>>> horses = [1, 2, 3, 4]
>>> races = itertools.permutations(horses)
>>> print(races)
<itertools.permutations object at 0xb754f1dc>
>>> print(list(itertools.permutations(horses)))
[(1, 2, 3, 4),
 (1, 2, 4, 3),
 (1, 3, 2, 4),
 (1, 3, 4, 2),
 (1, 4, 2, 3),
 (1, 4, 3, 2),
 (2, 1, 3, 4),
 (2, 1, 4, 3),
 (2, 3, 1, 4),
 (2, 3, 4, 1),
 (2, 4, 1, 3),
 (2, 4, 3, 1),
 (3, 1, 2, 4),
 (3, 1, 4, 2),
 (3, 2, 1, 4),
 (3, 2, 4, 1),
 (3, 4, 1, 2),
 (3, 4, 2, 1),
 (4, 1, 2, 3),
 (4, 1, 3, 2),
 (4, 2, 1, 3),
 (4, 2, 3, 1),
 (4, 3, 1, 2),
 (4, 3, 2, 1)]

Understanding the inner mechanisms of iteration

Iteration is a process implying iterables (implementing the __iter__() method) and iterators (implementing the __next__() method). Iterables are any objects you can get an iterator from. Iterators are objects that let you iterate on iterables.

There is more about it in this article about how for loops work.

key.description: Optional Stack Exchange application key. Raises the per-IP quota from 300 to 10,000 requests per day and unlocks pages above 25, which the API refuses anonymously. Keys are public identifiers, not secrets.

max.description: Upper bound on the sort field: score for `sort: votes`, Unix seconds for `activity` or `creation`. Not accepted with `relevance`.

tagged.description: Every tag must be present on the question.

value.name: CREAM CHEESE BRICK
value.story:
A brick, or a block: what's the difference? It seems like a negligible distinction, but we take such distinctions 
seriously-especially when it comes to Trader Joe's Cream Cheese.

Within the cheese biz, this particular presentation of Cream Cheese is known as a "brick." Brick, however, 
sounds heavy, and this creamy creation is anything but. Made for us using fresh milk and cream from cows not 
treated with rBST, it's everything you want cream cheese to be-rich, creamy, and when softened, quite spread-
able. So, rather than "brick," we'd like to refer to our Cream Cheese as a "block," as in "building block," since it 
can be a building block in so many delicious dishes.

What's that? You want examples? Sure. A simple appetizer idea: set it on a plate, top with salsa or sweet chili 
sauce and serve with tortilla chips or crackers for a Mexican or Thai inspired dip. How's that for instant versa-
tility? And speaking of dips, cream cheese is the star of any number of creamy dips. Don't forget bagels-but 
how could you forget bagels? Pretzel Bagels [sku 52370], maybe? Perhaps our favorite usage for this particular 
building block is cheesecake. If you're up to the challenge of making a cheesecake from scratch, you won't find 
a better foundation.

Perhaps the biggest WOW of all is our price of $1.69 for each eight-ounce block of certified kosher Trader Joe's 
Cream Cheese. You'll find it in our cheese case, next to other cream cheeses not in "block" form.

Made for us using fresh milk and cream from cows not treated with rBST, it’s everything you want cream cheese to be—rich, creamy, and when softened, quite spread- able. So, rather than “brick,” we’d like to refer to our Cream Cheese as a “block,” as in “building block,” since it can be a building block in so many delicious dishes.

What’s that? You want examples? Sure. A simple appetizer idea: set it on a plate, top with salsa or sweet chili sauce and serve with tortilla chips or crackers for a Mexican or Thai inspired dip. How’s that for instant versa- tility? And speaking of dips, cream cheese is the star of any number of creamy dips. Don’t forget bagels—but how could you forget bagels? Perhaps our favorite usage for this particular building block is cheesecake. If you’re up to the challenge of making a cheesecake from scratch, you won’t find a better foundation.

200.description:
One UniProtKB entry by accession (`P04637`), isoform accession (`P04637-2`), entry name (`P53_HUMAN`) or uniprot.org entry URL: recommended protein name with every synonym, gene names with synonyms, organism and lineage, curated function, subcellular location (per isoform, with topology and ECO evidence codes marking experimental, by-similarity or automatic assertions), GO terms with evidence, disease associations with OMIM numbers, sequence length and mass, and PDB, AlphaFold, ChEMBL, Ensembl, NCBI Gene and HGNC cross-references. Secondary (merged) accessions and entry names resolve to the current entry. Unknown and deleted accessions are `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| `annotation_score` | number | Annotation score, 1 (least) to 5 (best annotated); null when UniProt omits it. |
| `cross_references` | object |  |
| `diseases` | object[] | Curated disease associations (DISEASE comments). |
| `ec_numbers` | string[] | Enzyme Commission numbers. |
| `entry_name` | string | UniProtKB entry name (mnemonic), e.g. `P53_HUMAN`. |
| `entry_version` | number |  |

# GPT-4o

The "omni" model that unified text, audio, and vision in a single natively multimodal architecture, with audio response speeds averaging 320ms, a 16x improvement over prior voice pipeline approaches.

- **Model ID:** `openai/gpt-4o`
- **Type:** chat
- **Providers:** azure, openai
- **Context window:** 128,000
- **Maximum output tokens:** 16,384
- **Pricing:** $2.5/1M input tokens, $10.0/1M output tokens
- **Canonical page:** https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/gpt-4o

## Supported parameters

Detailed capability metadata has not been reported for this model.

## Example

```ts
import { streamText } from 'ai'

const result = streamText({
  model: 'openai/gpt-4o',
  prompt: 'Why is the sky blue?'
})
```

## About

GPT-4o was announced on May 13, 2024 at OpenAI's Spring Updates eve

post.description: Fetch one page of observations for a GHO indicator, filtered by spatial type (COUNTRY, REGION, WORLDBANKINCOMEGROUP, GLOBAL), ISO3/region codes, year range and Dim1/Dim2/Dim3 codes (sex, age group, ...). Each record keeps the source Id, numeric value with low/high bounds as decimal strings, the display string, comments, data source and modification date; source_updated_at is the indicator's newest modification date. Unknown indicator codes fail with not_found.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page of the same filters and page_size.

dim1.description: Dim1 value codes, e.g. SEX_FMLE or AGEGROUP_YEARS0-4.

indicator_code.description: GHO indicator code, e.g. WHOSIS_000001 (life expectancy at birth) or MDG_0000000001 (infant mortality rate). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]{1,64}$.

page_size.description:
Rows per page; the GHO server caps $top at 1000.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000; default 100.

spatial_dim_type.description:
Restrict to one spatial level. Omit for all levels; spatial_dim_type on each record says which.

Provider reference: allowed values ["COUNTRY", "REGION", "WORLDBANKINCOMEGROUP", "GLOBAL", "null"].

spatial_dims.description: ISO3 country codes (BRA), WHO region codes (AFR), income-group codes (WB_HI) or GLOBAL.

time_from.description:
Inclusive first year (TimeDim ge).

Provider reference: minimum 1000; maximum 9999.

time_to.description:
Inclusive last year (TimeDim le).

Provider reference: minimum 1000; maximum 9999.

value.body_html:
Here you'll find a list of hotfixes that address various issues related to World of Warcraft: Midnight, Mists of Pandaria Classic, Season of Discovery, Burning Crusade Classic, WoW Classic Era, and Hardcore. Some of the hotfixes below take effect the moment they were implemented, while others may require scheduled realm restarts to go into effect. Please keep in mind that some issues cannot be addressed without a client-side patch update. This list will be updated as additional hotfixes are applied.

Hotfixes

September 23, 2026

Classes

  • Death Knight
    • Unholy
      • Resolved an issue with Blightfall doing less damage as more time passes since the plague was applied.
  • Monk
    • Windwalker
      • Fixed an issue that caused PvP adjustments to Windwalker's Celestial Conduit and Flurry Strikes to apply in PvE as well.

Delves

  • Fixed issue where Valeera becomes unable to change talents and gain abilities after a faction change. Players experiencing this will need to enter a delve on the affected character, then leave the delve, and then log out to correct the issue.

September 22, 2026

Classes

  • Death Knight
    • Blood
      • Developers’ notes: San’layn is dealing quite a bit more damage in AoE than our intended target for tanks. We will be reducing their overall damage to reduce the disparity. However, we will be increasing Death Strike’s damage and reducing its cleave effectiveness to buff Blood’s single target wh

posts.body_html:
The Skyborne—also known as the shen’dorei, or hidden people—are a new playable race in World of Warcraft: Forever. Their journey begins on Zephras Isle, a level 1–12 starting experience that blends classic Warcraft aesthetics with elemental architecture and a story shaped by wind and ancestry. At character creation, you’ll choose whether your Skyborne joins the proud Horde or the noble Alliance.

View Full Article

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup: Why is this useless for a Rogue?

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup: Having 115 max damage, 1.9 speed, and it being main hand only kind of pooches it for combat rogues.  Remember, us combat rogues look for high max damage and slow speed weapons to hit off those nice sinister strikes.  However, if this was one-handed, i'd cry, and then get it for my off-hand.

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup: for the same reason Ashbringer sucks for a warrior; speed.

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup:
Don't forget that it not only does normal damage, but also Nature damage.
44 - 115 Damage	Speed 1.90
[b]+ 16 - 30 Nature Damage[/b]


Plus its Proc
[i]Chance On Hit: Blasts your enemy with lightning, dealing 300 Nature
damage and then jumping to additional nearby
enemies. Each jump reduces that victim's Nature
resistance by -25. Affects 5 targets. Your target
is also consumed by a cyclone, slowing its attack
speed by -25% for 12 seconds.[/i]

I wouldn't mind having this sword though.

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup: 3.0 speed on a 2 hander is decent .... and ashbringer rocks for any MS warrior

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup: No it doesn't. Even with 88 DPS, it gets inferior to slower weapons with lower DPS.

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup:
Like 1% of the server population seems to understand how attack power works.

Basically it's like this, the slower the weapon, no matter what it is, 1h, 2h, bow, etc, the higher the boost from attack power.  So a 50dps 2hander with a speed of 5, would outdamage a 80dps 2hander with a speed of 3 when it comes to instant attack specials like mortal strike.  Now the regular hits from the 80dps 2hander would make up a little ground, but not nearly enough to combat the huge bonus for slow weapons.

Point is, Ashbringer sucks for mortal strike warriors.  It's a dream weapon for a fury 2h warrior tho

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup: run the calculations.  +elemental damage is actually counted in with the DPS.

replies.author: Allakhazam
replies.body_markup:
1) It's a sword -- dagger types won't like the loss of abilities from it.

2)  It's damage is 44-115 so sword types, that use SS a lot, won't like the low SS yield from it.

3)  It's procs -- It's an AoE effect "up to 5 enemies" -- great... soloing you now can tank whatever's in the area when it goes off, grouping, let's see your tank keep aggro on a multi-pull with you using it, raiding -- etc...

In other words it'd be a nice main tank 1h weapon to help get the attention of everything in the area but for rogues, who rely on in-fighting, speedy attacks and NOT getting a lot of attention while

posts.author: ElhonnaDS
posts.body_markup:
Just a public service announcement- be careful how much information you give when friending people you don't know.  The Battletag system is anonymous, but a lot of times people will start phishing for e-mails, real names, facebook pages, etc.  They could just be super friendly, or they could be phishing for account info, or they could be mentally unstable people who you don't want to have that kind of info. 

That being said, I do have a number of battletag friends I met on wowhead, and it can be a great place to meet people.  But these were people who I knew from the forums for months or even years beforehand.  

On the other hand, I have given my battletag on an occasion or two to people who were really new and had a lot of questions, in an attempt to be a resource, and the results have been...interesting- lol. Certainly, if you don't give out any other info battletags are pretty harmless, though.

World of Warcraft: Forever brings massive changes to all classes, and for Retribution Paladin this is especially the case. Retribution is getting some desperately-needed love and attention, from new abilities and spells, to improvements & changes for existing ones. 

[pad]

[h2 type=bar toc="Changes in Forever"]Changes to Retribution Paladin in WoW Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]

Previously, Retribution Paladin was a rather weak class with little class identity and modest support offerings to raid and party members. Forever seeks to address these issues with the introduction of a revitalized talent tree, new spells & abilities, and has reworked existing ones to make them much more powerful and substantial. 

[h3 toc="New Abilities"]New Abilities and Talents in WoW Forever[/h3]

Of the new abilities and talents, the most interesting and impactful are surely [b]Holy Strike[/b] - our new instant attack which deals Holy damage - and [b]Twist of Light[/b], our current Retribution talent tree capstone that allows you to benefit from two seals on a single auto-attack by weaving back and forth between them. 

[center]
[table class=grid width=75%]

[tr][td width=20%]Spell[/td][td]Description[/td][/tr]

[tr][td][spell=10333][/td][td]A new instant attack that deals Holy damage based on weapon damage and spell power; similar to Crusader Strike. A new mainstay primary ability for damage-dealing. [/td][/tr]
[tr][td][spell=1310735][/td][td]The new capstone talent in the Retribution talent tree; allows you to "twist" back and forth between two seals to benefit from the effects of both on your melee attacks. When you switch seals, your previous seal gets turned into an "Echo" that will grant the effect of said seal on your next attack.[/td][/tr]
